prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of GLP-1 and of its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B045 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. All six round-1 files reach the same scientific judgment, and I have tried to test it rather than inherit it. The chain is continuous from the incretin effect and the physiology of native GLP-1 (Holst), through proglucagon-derived peptide biology, receptor action and the translational concept (Drucker), to identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), and on to a drug class with independent confirmation over about three decades and large randomized trials showing effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Maturity is not in question. On the chair's first question, I hold that the prize rewards the discovery and not the product, so the third place should go to the person whose work established what the active hormone is. On the second question, the citation can say that the discoveries made incretin-based therapies possible. That acknowledges the drugs without crediting their developers and without implying a fourth laureate. A single part is sufficient: I do not see a second part that is as mature, as clean in attribution and as clearly decided on scientific grounds, and a second part added to balance the prize would be the artificial completeness the protocol warns against.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and I have not resolved it. Habener is not among the credited names, the Mojsov, Habener and Holst priority history is contested, and none of us has audited it; the chair summary and several round-1 files say so, and I agree. If the attribution review finds that Mojsov's priority over Habener is not defensible, the third name would need to be reconsidered, and my trio would stand on Holst and Drucker alone with an open third place. The cap also excludes Knudsen, whose long-acting analogues are what reached patients, and a reader could see the prize as stopping short of the therapy. I accept that criticism as real. I judge it the lesser error, because the Committee's remit is the discovery. I also note that my round-1 recollection of the priority history is unverified and I do not claim more certainty than that.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen as a trio that runs from physiology to translation, treats Mojsov's credit as open, and would address the uncomfortable exclusion through the citation.
responses.response: I have taken this seriously and it is the strongest alternative to my trio. Where I agree: the exclusion of Knudsen is uncomfortable and the citation should not pretend the analogues did not matter. Where I still differ: swapping Mojsov for Knudsen changes what the prize is about, from the discovery of the active hormone to the engineering of a drug, and that is the distinction the Committee has to defend publicly. Commercial and clinical dominance of semaglutide and liraglutide should not stand in for scientific priority, a caution she herself raises. My answer to her wording concern is to place the therapeutic consequence in the citation, 'made possible incretin-based therapies', so that the analogue work is acknowledged without a name. I have not changed my view, but I would change it if the attribution review showed the active-peptide identification cannot be credited to Mojsov.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked the unfolded protein response (B007) first as a conceptually complete, mature two-person discovery by Walter and Mori, put GLP-1 third with Knudsen, and says the Mojsov credit is disputed.
responses.response: I agree that B007 is a clean two-name attribution and a fundamental advance, and I do not regard it as premature. It stays on my alternatives list. His own round-1 caveat is the reason I still place it behind B045: PERK, ATF6, Ron and Kaufman are outside the credited names, and the link to human disease is still largely preclinical or correlative. My answer to the chair's question on what evidence I would need is a validated therapeutic or diagnostic effect in patients that follows from the pathway itself. Until then, a prize on the pathway would be right on the science but early on benefit. On the Mojsov question, I accept that the priority is disputed. I do not accept that the dispute is settled by moving to the drug developer, as he proposes, and I would rather resolve it by the attribution review than by substitution. I have not been moved on B007 or on Knudsen. I also disclose that I have co-authored with him, so my disagreement should be read with that in mind and not as deference.

responses.point: Sandberg ranks GLP-1 first, treats Mojsov's identification of the active peptide as decisive but contested, names Knudsen as a possible substitute, and doubts that a two-person CAR-T credit (June, Sadelain) is as safe as a three-person one.
responses.response: I agree with his caution that high opening agreement does not equal merit, since we may all be reading the same recollection of the same history, and with his view that the priority claims have not been audited. That is the main reason I keep the Mojsov place described as a judgment and not a fact. I differ in that I would keep Mojsov over Knudsen even on a contested record, because a contested priority claim for the discovery still outranks an uncontested development claim for the drug under our remit. On CAR-T, his point about Rosenberg and Eshhar has moved me in one respect: I now think a two-person June and Sadelain prize would be harder to defend than the three-name version, and if B016 is ever the second part I would want Rosenberg retained. That keeps CAR-T as my first alternative and not a preferred part.

responses.point: El Manira supports a physiology-led trio of Holst, Drucker and Mojsov as the people who established what the hormone is and does, treats Knudsen's work as industrial development, and warns that if the Committee reads the discovery as the drug the trio is wrong.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on the principle. I take his warning about the opposite reading as a real risk and not a rhetorical one: if colleagues conclude the discovery is the drug, then Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, or a different framing, is the right answer, and Mojsov's place would not survive. I would not try to hide that dependency. In my view the right response is to make the principle explicit in the citation and in the public statement, which is why I favour wording that names the physiology and the active peptide and then states the therapeutic consequence. I do not agree with him that the commercial-product concern needs more than that, because the evidence base is academic physiology and large independent trials.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority over Habener and Holst for the active peptide survives an actual audit of the record, which no member has done and I have not done.
Whether the Committee agrees that the prize is for the discovery and not the drug, since that principle alone decides between Mojsov and Knudsen.
Whether a single prize part is better than a second part, and if a second part is added, whether CAR-T (B016) needs Rosenberg named to be defensible.
Whether B007 will have disease-relevant evidence strong enough to move ahead of CAR-T as the second part in a later year.

My description of my own round-1 ranking differs from how some colleagues summarised it, and the chair summary and the member files do not agree on every detail; I rely on my own file and the shortlist.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I have co-authored roughly twenty works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy), unrelated to any shortlisted ballot, and I have said above that this should not make me defer to him or prevent me from disagreeing. I worked with Paul Greengard as a postdoctoral fellow; he is not credited on any shortlisted ballot. As a neurologist I have only a field-level link to B004 (optogenetics) and B035 (SMN2 antisense), not a personal tie. I do not request recusal.
